clue.text: America's first couple on aircraft discarded material

indicators.note: on in an across clue means coming after, as if added on to the end

parts.note: jets are aircraft, here in the plural

indicators.note: the first couple of letters of the word America's are taken

explanation.surface: The President and First Lady arrive by plane, amid talk of things thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First couple' looks like the presidential pair, but it means the opening two letters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship, hence discarded stuff generally.

clue.text: Playwright, for audience, author of meaningful work?

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: Ben Jonson was an English Jacobean playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist, writing for theatregoers, whose work carries meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson compiled the great 1755 Dictionary, a work literally full of meanings; Ben Jonson's surname is spelt without the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's famous work was his Dictionary, a book of word meanings.

clue.text: Thatcher's rival, so-called? Leading rebel

indicators.note: so-called here means named as spoken, pointing to a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a roofer who lays tiles competes with one who thatches roofs: a tiler

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a challenger to Margaret Thatcher who led a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher looks like the Prime Minister, but it is a roof thatcher. Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler was the chief figure of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt, a famous insurgent leader.

clue.text: GOP argues falsely they break people down

indicators.note: falsely means the letters of the words are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Republican Party members argue dishonestly, and the result crushes people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break down' means categorise, not crush or distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Demographic bands such as 18 to 24 divide a population into categories by years lived.

clue.text: Kind of desk disreputable female just needs time to shift

indicators.note: the time letter is told to shift its place within the word

parts.note: a trollop is an old insulting word for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A sly comment on which desk suits a woman of bad reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving TROLLOP's first T to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolltop desk has a slatted flexible cover that rolls down over the writing surface.

clue.text: After briefly not working, a head is in school again

indicators.note: after places the second part behind the first
briefly means the word is cut short, keeping only its opening

parts.note: someone retired is no longer working
each means a head, as in five pounds per head

explanation.surface: A head teacher back from a break is in school once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' reads as a headteacher but means EACH (per head); RETIRED cut short gives RET.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to instruct them; to do so a second time is to give the lessons again.

clue.text: First or last name, or character of Oxford writer

definitions.meaning: a name used both as a forename, ... Carroll, and as a surname, C. S. ...
Inspector Morse's sergeant in Colin Dexter's Oxford detective novels

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how an Oxford author is named, or what personality they have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests personality, but means a figure in fiction: Sergeant Lewis in Colin Dexter's Morse books, set in Oxford. Lewis Carroll and C. S. Lewis were both Oxford writers too.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is a forename and a surname, and the sidekick of Dexter's detective Morse.

clue.text: Driver may change into this kind of party clothing

parts.note: a third party is one beyond the two main sides
gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: A motorist may slip into this outfit for a certain kind of party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change into' suggests putting on clothes, but it is a gear change.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's gearbox has numbered ratios, and a motorist shifts up or down into the next one.

clue.text: Knight, say, capturing rook to make a breakthrough

indicators.note: capturing means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: a knight is an example of a chess piece
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move in which a knight takes a rook and breaks through.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to bore through something, punching a hole in it.

clue.text: Astronomer has star confused with this star, oddly

indicators.note: confused means the letters are jumbled; together with star they make up astronomer

explanation.surface: A stargazer muddles one star with another.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of Astronomer, jumbled, are STAR plus the answer. 'Oddly' because Marilyn Monroe, a film star, stands among a grid of US presidents (James Monroe was one too).
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was a Hollywood screen celebrity, and the surname is also that of the fifth US president.

clue.text: Provided with assistance, having shaped up the dole

indicators.note: shaped means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone got benefits by reshaping the welfare system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped up' looks like a phrasal verb, but up is fodder alongside THE DOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone out is to give them aid in a difficulty.

clue.text: It parallels Number Ten — as its occupants do in today's solutions

definitions.text: It parallels Number Ten — as its occupants do in today's solutions

parts.words: It parallels Number Ten — as its occupants do in today's solutions
parts.note: Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's home; its US equivalent is the President's residence, and presidents fill the grid

explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's official residence. Many answers in the grid are US presidents' surnames, the occupants of the American counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: The President's Washington residence plays the role that Downing Street plays in Britain.

clue.text: More confident as litigant, suppressing resistance

indicators.note: suppressing means holding the other part down inside

parts.note: one who sues is a suer
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A litigant gains confidence by quelling opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Surer is the comparative of sure, meaning more certain.

clue.text: Like some music or, perhaps after initial cuts, like some poetry

indicators.note: the word perhaps is used after its opening letters are cut away

parts.note: odic means of or like an ode

explanation.surface: Deciding whether something is musical or, with some trimming, poetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is just a link; PERHAPS losing its first two letters gives RHAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free, emotional musical composition, so the adjective describes such pieces.

clue.text: Write backing melody for final movement of suite

indicators.note: backing means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Instructions to compose a backing tune for the last part of a suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing melody' reads as accompaniment, but backing reverses PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's orchestral suite The Planets closes with the movement for the eighth planet.

clue.text: Sets about Republican involved with hard copies

indicators.note: about means going around the other parts

parts.note: to set something is to put it
into means keen on or involved with

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a Republican handling printed documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper output from a computer printer is called hard copy, as opposed to on-screen versions.

clue.text: Clean house again

parts.note: over means again, as in do it over

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy the house once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean house' reads as one phrase, but house gives HO.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoover is the British verb for vacuum-cleaning, from the brand of vacuum cleaner.

clue.text: Reds fan, perhaps, I help when distressed after 1-0 upset

indicators.note: after places the second part behind the first
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: the score one-nil, read as ONE and O

indicators.note: distressed means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Liverpool supporter, troubled by a one-nil defeat, wants to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds fan' suggests a football supporter (Liverpool are the Reds), but it means a lover of red wines. ONEO reversed is OENO; I HELP rearranged is PHILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of wine might well love clarets and other red varieties.

clue.text: Predecessor of 1 down on both sides of the pond

definitions.text: Predecessor of 1 down on both sides of the pond

parts.words: Predecessor of 1 down on both sides of the pond
parts.note: Harold ... was a British Prime Minister before Boris Johnson, and Woodrow ... a US President before Lyndon or Andrew Johnson

explanation.walkthrough: The pond is the Atlantic: the name belongs to a British Prime Minister (Harold) and an American President (Woodrow), each earlier than a leader with 1 down's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Britain and America had a leader of this surname who held office before a Johnson did.

clue.text: No Trump action about WMD material? He's crazy

indicators.note: about means going around the next part

parts.note: NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps
uranium, chemical symbol U, is material for nuclear weapons of mass destruction
a case is a legal action

explanation.surface: Seems to say there is no court case against Trump over weapons, so someone is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No Trump' looks like politics but is the bridge bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is a slang term for a mad person.

clue.text: Like position of moderate, as shown in recent rally

indicators.note: shown in means the letters are displayed within the following words

explanation.surface: A recent political rally reveals where a moderate stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderate stands in the middle of the political spectrum, neither left nor right.

clue.text: Driver of one vehicle or another over short period

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first part above the second

parts.note: another vehicle is a car

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone drives one vehicle or another for a little while.
explanation.definitionFit: A carter drives a cart, a horse-drawn vehicle for goods.

clue.text: Line in column on Northern or Eastern city

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the previous part above the next

explanation.surface: A line in a newspaper column about some northern or eastern city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is a cathedral city in the east of England, county town of Lincolnshire.

clue.text: Top man in legendary dining circle

definitions.text: Top man in legendary dining circle

parts.words: Top man in legendary dining circle
parts.note: the legendary king who presided over his knights at the Round Table

explanation.walkthrough: The dining circle is the Round Table of Camelot; Chester Arthur was also a US President, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: King of Camelot, he headed the knights who sat at the Round Table.

clue.text: Muscle 19 down turned to right

indicators.note: turned means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, a driver of a cart

explanation.surface: A muscle turned 19 down towards the right.
explanation.walkthrough: CARTER turned is RETRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a muscle that draws a body part back in.

clue.text: Bring up a time and a place for spectacle

indicators.note: bring up in a down clue means lift the letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Suggesting a time and venue for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is just a link; AN ERA reversed upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue for sports and shows, originally the sanded floor of a Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: Some propagandist not operating in good faith?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A propagandist acting dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good faith' means honestly, but here it means inside a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen stands outside the mainstream religious faiths, with the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: Allow wild speech supporting head of government

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts this part underneath the first
the head of the word government is its first letter

parts.note: a rant is a wild, angry speech

explanation.surface: A wild speech propping up the head of government is tolerated.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a request is to permit or concede it.

clue.text: See 10
Article Cameron edited, consuming one kind of coffee

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: consuming means taking the next part inside
edited means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: David Cameron's piece gets edited while he drinks a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMERON rearranged gives MERCANO, which takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water.

clue.text: Phrase otherwise concerning Washington, for example

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
Washington is a US state

explanation.surface: A rewording about Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington looks like the capital, but it is the state.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in other words is to express it again.

clue.text: Not conversant with name for a mathematician and physicist

parts.note: being new to something means not yet familiar with it

explanation.surface: Someone unfamiliar with the name of a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton formulated gravitation and the laws of motion and co-invented calculus.
